This is a thanksgiving tale

This thanksgiving was the first time I brought a girlfriend to meet the relatives. She was nervous that they wouldn't like her, but for the most part they're easygoing people and I assured her it would be fine. However, these are heavyset southern people who are serious about their food, and it did not take long for that to become obvious.

Background

I started my thanksgiving break about 2 weeks into a lean bulk bulk after a successful cut to ~10% bodyfat, so I'm still a pretty lean 6'2"/175lbs. Girlfriend is 5'2"/115lbs and is trying a slow cut because she's close to her strength goals in the gym. We decided to go easy for thanksgiving and not count macros/calories on MyFitnessPal like usual (170 day streak both). My solution was to take a Keto approach to prevent overeating and to focus on consuming as much protein as comfortable to prevent wasting if I don't make it on calories for some reason. Girlfriend didn't have a particular approach, just planned on eating around 300 calories per meal and to never eat anything she didn't like from the first bite.

The Start of Problems

The problems became noticeable from the first breakfast. We helped set up and were told to sit, while my mother and aunt distributed food. They gave my girlfriend and myself equal portions of food, adding up to about 400 calories of pure carbs. I frowned and my girlfriend made a boasting face that she deserved more than I, and it wasn't until much later that she realized that she had messed up her typical macros pretty badly and didn't want to eat. She offered me a bit off her plate and I noted that this was met with a scowl from my aunt. I think that she and my mother had some strange idea of equality of portion size, even though my girlfriend and I have very different goals and bodies(ffs my chest is almost twice the width of here). This behavior of giving her and I identical portions of food continued for every home cooked meal that we ate for the rest of the trip, and was continued by my mother in my aunt's absence.

At thanksgiving dinner with my father's side of the family I got rather drunk, ate rather unhealthily, and was rather dangerously vocal in my opinions. Dangerous not only because there were 18 month olds in the vicinity but also because my self, brother, and girlfriend are the only people of healthy weight in my family. My cousin Josh used to be skinny fat in highschool and we thought he'd muscle up when he joined the Marines. Unfortunately, he came back looking as soft as when he left and in the last year his beer belly has grown into a flabby panda physique of around 20% body fat. The rest of my relatives range between 30% and 40% body fat. At least they're generally nice, amicable people but I have learned well to never fully relax.

Discussion went from changes in society (damn the Frankfurt School) to politics (power is a tricky thing, but maybe we'll maga) and finally to health. I've been interested in a few different theories recently so I thought I'd have something to say. I expressed that I was distrustful of fake sweeteners for cheapening what should be an occasional treat, and postulated that the only truly healthy part of fruit was the fiber, which would disqualify bananas as a health food. At the time I was eating anything with fat or protein in it and am well known for doing the same thing almost every time I come home, so I was hit with plenty of "if I had your metabolism"'s and the like and wasn't feeling like having it. I foolishly told my family that they could tell me I was eating unhealthy when they get where I am by eating the way they typically do. I got silence and scowls but the conversation moved on and hopefully I won't have to deal with any ill will next year.

tl;dr: salty about girlfriend having excessive amounts of carbs thrust in front of her and about being called out for eating unhealthily around a bunch of fat relatives when I'm holiday splurging.

Been lurking here since this forum was created, I think. Posting now because I was talking to someone on discord about what we need to legitimize this investigation, and we decided on a type of wiki. The general idea is the following:

The main wiki page will have:

  1. A list of 'official' claims that the investigation is currently making

  2. A link to a list of 'personal' claims that the investigation is also considering

What makes a personal claim not official is a lack of supporting evidence and lack of peer review. So ultimately as going from personal to official is a qualitative process, it should occur on this voat forum.

Each official claim has a main landing page with a overview of the claim and its general merits. This overview can be as long as necessary so long as it is properly formatted. We should think of these landing pages as containing all the necessary information that would be needed in a courtroom argument (or rather, that is what we're striving towards). As such we should try to formalize these arguments (as in, with formal logic). It will also contain a list to all the auxiliary pages whose topics are elements that the claim draws upon for a proposition in its argument. The benchmark for what it means for a claim to satisfy this requirement is the following:

  • On the auxiliary page we will create a subheading with the title being the name of the specific claim

  • We should be able to write, underneath this subheading, at least a paragraph explaining why the topic of the auxiliary page is relevant/important to the argument of the claim

This is also where another key difference between personal and official claims is seen. On auxiliary pages, subheadings should only be created for official claims. The reason is that otherwise the pages would be swamped with essays from personal claims, which we don't even take as credible enough to label as 'official'. The point of this wiki is to present the information in an organized and accessible way. With this in mind, clarity and accuracy are the most important values we should have.

The last thing I want to touch on is how to create personal theories. Anyone can do it, but I think that they should have to make a basic account (no email address or anything needed, just an ID through which all their theories can be indexed). So you click on the "personal theories" link on the main wiki page, and then you get perhaps a shortlist of the theories with the most threads that have the theory linked, and then a list of user IDs embedded with a link to that users' list of personal theories. This will also help people organize their own theories so that they can present them to the forum in a standardized way.

In conclusion the wiki will be made up of: the main landing page, official claims' landing pages, auxiliary pages, the personal claims' list, users' claims lists, and personal claims' landing pages.

The early stages of creating a well structured wiki for all the investigations' findings can begin as soon as we start presenting our information aggregated into claims this way. Two things I want to have a discussion on in this thread:

  1. The purposed structure of this wiki

  2. The way in which we should compile the list and supporting evidence for all of our current claims
